title: Introduce 'SimLab' quickstart: lightweight RAG scenario authoring + telemetry playground
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Added SimLab quickstart: a lightweight authoring + telemetry playground for RAG scenarios. Includes local-run scripts, example prompts, and built-in probes for latency/cost assertions.
description:
Summary: Add 'SimLab' quickstart for developers to author, run, and iterate on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) scenarios locally with minimal setup. The quickstart focuses on fast feedback loops: scenario step assertions, lightweight telemetry probes (latency, token cost, assertion pass rate), and a compact runner that can replay synthetic user sessions for testing and evals. Motivation: teams repeatedly ask for a minimal example that bridges docs and examples — not a full authoring studio but richer than a single README. This PR introduces a single opinionated, reproducible sandbox that can be used for authoring, CI smoke checks, and onboarding.

What this includes (single-line summary): docs/quickstarts/simlab/README.md, example corpora, prebuilt telemetry probes, a local sim runner (node + python shims), structured-output assertion examples, and CI smoke manifest.

Checklist:
- [x] Quickstart narrative and step-by-step README
- [x] Compact starter corpus and index script
- [x] Local sim runner with configurable concurrency and seedable randomness
- [x] Telemetry probe harness (latency, token-cost, assertion pass rates)
- [x] CI smoke job example (docs smoke) and link-checker integration
- [x] Example prompts + structured-output lint examples
- [ ] Integration with the authoring web UI (follow-up: ENG-2346)

Compatibility notes: the runner targets the Redwood API but falls back to a local mock shim (for offline demos). The telemetry probes emit JSONL telemetry suitable for ingestion into the console or for local analysis via simlab/telemetry/parse.py.

How to try locally (abridged):
1) cd docs/quickstarts/simlab
2) ./bootstrap.sh  # installs minimal node/python deps, creates test-index
3) ./run-sim --scenario sample-ticket --replay 5 --concurrency 1
4) ./telemetry/collect.sh  # runs built-in probes and prints pass/fail summary

Design decisions (brief):
- Keep API surface intentionally small: single README, one run script, and a telem probe harness so teams can copy the pattern into CI.
- Use JSONL for telemetry to avoid schema coupling; telemetry/parse.py contains a small mapping to convert to the Console ingest format for deeper analysis.
- Make prompts and assertions explicit (assertion files live under scenarios/ and are YAML-like) so regressions are actionable.

Related: ENG-2345 (SimLab spec), PM-98 (onboarding improvements), SUP-421 (customer ask for local scenario replay), docs: #authoring-playbooks

review_thread: Ethan Brooks: Nice focused quickstart. A few UX nits: can we reduce bootstrap time and make the runner skip index rebuild if index exists?
Priya Kapoor: Good call — added a cache check in bootstrap.sh and updated README to document --skip-index. Also added explicit step to seed randomness for deterministic replays.
Lina Park: Telemetry parse script looks fine but add a unit test for latency percentiles calculation; otherwise LGTM.
Priya Kapoor: Added a small pytest for telemetry/parse.py in the last commit.
Noor Ali: sre note — ensure the sim runner respects RPS limits by default and has a --dry-run flag to validate config. Also requested clearer failure exit codes for CI.
Priya Kapoor: Implemented --dry-run and exit codes (0 success, 2 assertion failure, 3 telemetry threshold breach). Updated docs with CI example that fails the job when thresholds are exceeded.
merge_summary: Merged by squash on 2026-02-13 by Lina Park. Commit message: docs(simlab): add SimLab quickstart with runner and telemetry probes — closes ENG-2345, PM-98. Merge method: squash and merge.
notes_for_reviewers: This is intended to be a minimalist surface — follow-ups will add a playground UI and CI templating. Please focus on reproducibility and clarity in the README (we expect this to be used verbatim by SEs in onboarding).
testing_instructions: See description 'How to try locally' and run ci/docs-smoke/simlab-smoke.yaml with the test token. The smoke job will run the sim, collect telemetry, and return a non-zero exit when thresholds fail.
